title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Use a shared six-round divider in execute
motivation:
The 5.442 MHz baseline has a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through forwarding,
execute and the ALU into the timed data-memory logic. The ALU infers
combinational division and remainder for both signed and unsigned inputs,
making them the leading suspect for the long ALU path. The baseline
Verilator retirement trace reproduced all 4,491,485 marker-bracketed
cycles with both bus stalls active and contained zero DIV or REM family
instructions inside that window. Both DIVU retirements were outside it.
Sharing and registering division can cut ALU delay and area while adding
execution cycles only to those four operations.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
In the existing EX stage, capture the forwarded operands and run one unsigned
restoring divider for six cycles of six radix-2 steps each. Prepend four
zero bits to the 32-bit dividend magnitude so every round can reuse the
same datapath. Each step shifts a dividend bit into the partial remainder,
uses a widened subtract and its borrow to select the next remainder, and
emits one quotient bit. Register quotient and remainder state each round.

quotient and the dividend sign for a remainder. Preserve divide-by-zero
and INT_MIN / -1 results. Use eight EX cycles with an advancing MEM stage,
including operand capture, six rounds and completion. Keep the same
sequence in ALTOPS with the existing stand-in results.

during the divide. Snapshot operands at issue and hold the completed result
until EX/MEM accepts it exactly once. The ordinary EX/MEM bypass then

start marker. Compare marker-bracketed cycles and median Gowin Fmax against

the +50% estimate and about 5.70 MHz clears the acceptance margin. Use the
new Gowin path report to check that the long combinational ALU path is
gone, and run the existing correctness gates.

implementation_notes:
# Shared six-round divider

The EX ALU now shares one unsigned restoring divider across DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU. It captures the forwarded operands, runs six rounds of six radix-2 steps, and transfers the result on the eighth EX cycle when MEM can advance. The divider registers the partial remainder and reuses a 36-bit shift register for the padded dividend and outgoing quotient bits. ALTOPS captures the existing stand-in result and uses the same handshake and latency.

The divider derives signed results from unsigned magnitudes. A zero divisor naturally leaves the dividend magnitude in the remainder and produces an all-ones quotient. Sign restoration preserves the original dividend for a zero-divisor remainder and skips quotient negation in that case. The 32-bit magnitude and result also preserve `INT_MIN / -1` and its zero remainder.

Fetch and decode hold while EX waits. When MEM advances during the divide, EX/MEM captures a bubble with inactive controls, letting older instructions retire. A divide captures its forwarded values for RVFI at issue and passes through EX/MEM once, where the usual bypass serves the next instruction. The core retains its single-channel RVFI interface.

A guarded include brings the core-wide types into scope for the requested alphabetical Verilator glob. Fetch flush is driven independently of the load-use check to remove Verilator's apparent feedback path in VPI builds.

## Local checks

- Strict Verilator lint passed in hardware and ALTOPS modes.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-channel ALTOPS checks with zero failures. The deep arithmetic suite was outside this run. Cocotb and cosim exercised the hardware arithmetic.
- `make test TARGET=bench` passed all five cocotb runners. Divider coverage includes exact completion latency, delayed acceptance, consecutive requests, reset during a divide, and signed and unsigned edge cases. The pipeline regression checks retirement order and forwarding through a stalled older load.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` passed all five ELFs. Selftest and three random programs matched the ISS with and without bus stalls. CoreMark passed all CRC checks with both stalls active.

## Gowin and CoreMark

| Metric | Baseline | Shared divider |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Marker-bracketed cycles | 4,491,485 | 4,491,485 |
| Median Fmax, MHz | 5.442 | 42.123 |
| CoreMark iterations per second | 12.12 | 93.78 |
| Gowin logic cells | 12,312 | 2,773 |
| Gowin registers | 460 | 565 |

`NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench` measured 41.866, 42.123 and 42.123 MHz across the three placement options. Equal bracketed cycles yield 7.74× baseline throughput. The option-0 worst setup path runs between two divider remainder registers, with 29.180 ns of data arrival time. All three options place their worst setup path within the divider. The baseline 199.837 ns forwarding-to-data-memory path is no longer the limiting path. [Gowin option-0 report](cores/bench/generated/gowin_p0/impl/pnr/core_bench.tr)

The eight-cycle EX occupancy adds seven cycles per divide without backpressure, so workloads that frequently divide can lose cycles relative to the prior single-cycle execution. The six-step divider round now limits Fmax.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-001-r1s0 (regression, +673.76%): Replacing combinational DIV/REM with a shared, registered restoring divider moved the critical path from EX-to-memory logic into the six-step divider round, raising median Gowin Fmax from 5.442 to 42.123 MHz while the divide-free CoreMark window avoided the extra EX cycles.

title: Share a registered execute-stage divider for DIV and REM
motivation: The bench retest reaches 5.442 MHz and reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through EX forwarding and the ALU to the data-memory path. The ALU feeds its common result mux with four combinational division and remainder expressions. The depth of an unrolled divider makes it the leading suspect for the low clock rate, and the mux exposes its delay even on cycles issuing ordinary instructions. A baseline Verilator retirement trace with both bus stalls enabled and all CoreMark CRCs validated counted zero DIV/REM instructions and 93,960 MUL instructions in the 4,491,485-cycle timed interval.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the four combinational DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU implementations with one blocking, registered divider in EX. On launch, capture operand magnitudes and sign controls, then compute 32 quotient bits over seven registered restoring-division updates, with two bit steps in the first update and five in each of the next six. Each step shifts in one dividend bit, uses a 33-bit trial subtract to choose the next partial remainder, and appends the corresponding quotient bit. Select the quotient or remainder after the last update, apply the appropriate sign for signed operations, and transfer it through the usual EX/MEM boundary. Handle zero divisors and INT_MIN divided by -1 with their exact RV32M results on the same schedule. Keep multiply and RV32I on the single-cycle ALU path so matrix multiplication, address generation and ordinary dependencies incur no new EX latency.

Launch once from a valid divide/remainder in ID/EX when the older memory stage can advance. Hold IF and ID/EX during the divide and insert EX/MEM bubbles after the older instruction advances, so older work drains exactly once. Capture the original forwarded operands at launch for RVFI and retain the result until EX/MEM accepts it. The completed instruction forwards and retires through the existing in-order path. Keep the same launch, wait and completion schedule in ALTOPS mode with the existing substitute results. With both buses ready, eight added EX cycles plus one possible load-use or redirect bubble give at most ten cycles between consecutive retirements, within the unchanged liveness check window.

The experiment predicts a shorter Gowin critical path and fewer LUTs. The baseline trace implies zero direct divider waits inside the timed interval. Its two DIVU instructions outside that interval can shift the bus-stall sequence relative to the start marker, so measure the cycle count again. At the baseline cycle count, about 5.70 MHz median Gowin Fmax clears the acceptance threshold and 8.17 MHz gives approximately 50 percent higher fitness. Compare the new worst path delay and cell count against the retest and score the measured Fmax and validated CoreMark cycle count together.

title: Predict branches and jumps with a 16-entry tagged BTB
motivation:
Fetch and decode share a cycle in this core. Every taken branch or jump
currently discards one fetch slot while EX supplies the target. CoreMark's
repeated loop backedges and jump sites can reuse resolved targets and
recover those slots even with the existing instruction bus stalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 16-entry direct-mapped branch target buffer for conditional branches
and both jump opcodes, JAL and JALR. Index by PC[5:2] and match PC[19:6]
for aligned fetch PCs below 1 MiB. Each entry holds an 18-bit target word
address and a two-bit saturating direction counter. On a taken miss,
allocate at weakly taken. On a matching conditional branch, train the
counter toward its resolved direction and refresh the target when taken.
For either jump opcode, store the last resolved target as strongly taken.
Keep sequential fetch on misses and on hits whose counter predicts
fall-through. This puts a tag check and a mux on the fetch PC path.

Apply the prediction only when IF/ID is accepted into ID/EX. During the
following EX cycle, the fetch PC is already that instruction's predicted
successor and holds there if an older data access stalls EX. On a valid
EX advance, compare that PC with the full resolved architectural next PC
for every instruction. On a mismatch, redirect and squash the younger
instruction, even when instruction memory is unready. Train once on EX
advance using the hit and counter captured when the instruction was
accepted. If the same acceptance edge writes the fetched index, compare
the fetch tag against the written tag for the captured hit and capture
the written counter. Use the stored entry to select the predicted PC.
This uses one lookup per cycle and preserves saturation on adjacent
updates. Preserve EX's misalignment trap handling and report the resolved
next PC through RVFI. Recover when JALR resolves to a different target.

The scratch prototype reduced bracketed CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485
to 4,215,937 with both bus stalls enabled and passed the UART and CRC
checks. Median Gowin Fmax was 5.438 MHz across the three placement
options, yielding 12.899 iterations per second, a 6.42% gain over 12.12.
The prototype passed all 53 single-retire formal checks and the RVFI
reference comparisons with and without bus stalls.

implementation_notes:
# 16-entry tagged branch target buffer

## Implementation

- IF indexes the BTB with fetch PC bits [5:2] and checks the [19:6] tag for aligned PCs below 1 MiB. Conditional branches allocate on a taken miss at weakly taken and train a saturating two-bit counter on a hit. JAL and JALR cache the last representable target at strongly taken. Only valid bits require table reset.
- IF selects the successor from the stored entry when ID accepts the instruction. A same-index EX update supplies the captured counter and tag match for training that instruction on its own EX advance. The captured state holds across data stalls.
- EX compares the registered fetch PC with the full resolved successor on every valid advance. A mismatch squashes the younger instruction and redirects even with imem unready. An older data-memory hold defers both recovery and training. RVFI reports the same resolved successor, including PC+4 on a misaligned target trap.
- EX sends compact source and target word addresses after checking BTB eligibility. A taken target outside the BTB range uses full-width recovery and leaves the previous entry available. JALR clears target bit zero before alignment checking or training.
- The guarded include in `core.sv` makes the requested alphabetical RTL glob work with Verilator. Bench uses the single-retirement channel defined in its `core.yaml`.

## Validation

- The requested Verilator lint command and `make lint TARGET=bench` passed without warnings.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-retirement ALTOPS checks on the first run.
- `make test TARGET=bench` passed all five cocotb runners, including directed cases for adjacent training, index collisions, stale predictions, and JALR recovery with simultaneous bus backpressure and a later misaligned target.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench` passed with `NRET=1`. Selftest and three random programs matched the RVFI reference with and without bus stalls. CoreMark passed all UART and CRC checks under both stalls and ran 4,215,937 bracketed cycles, down 6.13% from the supplied baseline.
- Gowin measured 5.179, 5.521, and 5.521 MHz for placement options 0, 1, and 2. The 5.521 MHz median gives 13.096 CoreMark iterations per second, up 8.05% from the supplied 12.12 baseline.

## Timing and area

The BTB adds a tag check and target mux to the fetch PC path. The worst reported paths still traverse the EX ALU, with placement option 0 reporting 12,911 logic cells, 479 registers, and 17 LUT-RAM cells for the timed design.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-003-r1s2 (regression, +8.09%): With combinational DIV/REM in EX still limiting the clock to 5.5 MHz, the 16-entry tagged BTB's 6.1% CoreMark cycle savings from reusing taken branch and jump targets under bus stalls were too small to close the throughput gap to the 47.0 MHz registered-divider variant.

title: Squash decode through the ID/EX valid bit
motivation:
The registered-divider champion reaches 46.963 MHz and reports a 27.746 ns
setup path from the ID/EX source register through forwarding, EX, IF and
hazard control back to an ID/EX control register. EX redirect currently
selects a replacement instruction in IF and clears the wide ID/EX payload.
That puts late branch resolution on instruction decode, load-use matching
and a high-fanout payload clear. The same squash can be expressed by changing
only the validity of the decode slot.

pipeline depth and redirect latency.

load-use check with ID/EX validity and fetch readiness, keeping the current
source-register match policy. On EX/MEM advance, qualify mem_read, mem_write
and the post-trap reg_write with `id_ex.valid && !div_wait`. The resulting
controls protect memory requests, hazard detection and forwarding from
invalid slots. During a dmem stall, keep the held MEM/WB writer eligible for
bypass after its retirement valid bit clears.

exceed about 49.12 MHz to clear the 4.6% acceptance margin. The 12% estimate

path through IF and hazard control into the ID/EX decode payload is gone, and
use the measured cycle count and median Fmax to score the result. A remaining
EX-to-PC path or the five-step divider update could become the frequency limit.

implementation_notes:
# Squash decode through the ID/EX valid bit

## Implementation

- IF passes the raw instruction and `io_imemReady` to ID. Data backpressure and divider wait hold both ID/EX payload and validity. On advance, ID/EX captures the payload and sets validity to `imem_ready && !load_use && !redirect`. Reset clears the valid bit.
- Load-use detection requires a valid EX load and a ready fetch and compares both raw source register fields against the nonzero load destination. Redirect goes directly from EX to the PC and ID/EX valid bit. A redirect takes priority over a PC hold.
- EX requires a valid instruction for redirect and divider launch. On EX/MEM advance, memory controls and post-trap register write are qualified by `id_ex.valid && !div_wait`. The retained MEM/WB register-write control keeps its result eligible for bypass across a data stall after its retirement valid clears.
- The final implementation also shares the resolved EX target between the PC, alignment check, and RVFI next-PC. Branches and JAL use the PC-relative sum, and JALR uses the forwarded base plus immediate with bit 0 cleared. IF expresses redirect and sequential advance as a single PC update enable. This version measured a 49.128 MHz median after the initial valid-bit implementation measured 49.003 MHz.
- Directed cocotb cases drive valid store, jump, and load words on unready fetches and place each on a taken branch's discarded path. A discarded divide also checks that invalid EX slots cannot delay target issue. The tests check redirect priority across both bus holds, forwarded branch operands, the first target retirement and result, contiguous RVFI order, all data-bus requests, and exactly one acceptance of the stalled older store.

## Local verification

- Verilator lint passed with `-Wall` and no warnings.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 checks on the final RTL in a scratch checkout layout under `$TMPDIR`. It auto-selected the single-retirement wrapper and ALTOPS checks. Zero formal failures and zero formal fix attempts.
- All five pytest runners for the bench cocotb suite passed, including the new pipeline cases.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1` passed selftest with and without stalls and the stalled CoreMark CRC checks. The Makefile's local build needs `NRET=1` explicitly because the cosim build script defaults to two channels.

## Gowin timing and CoreMark

`make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1` measured **109.38 iterations/s** from 10 iterations over **4,491,485 marker-bracketed cycles**. The placement options measured 47.515, 49.128, and 49.128 MHz, with **49.128 MHz** median. The cycle count matched the champion. Fitness rose **4.61%** from 104.56 iterations/s, clearing the 4.6% margin by about **0.005 MHz**. Option 0 used 2,769 logic cells and 563 registers.

Within ID/EX, redirect and load-use feed only the valid bit. The payload's capture enable depends on data backpressure and divider wait. The former EX-to-IF-to-hazard path into the ID/EX payload is absent from the worst setup paths. The median options are limited by the five-step divider update from `partial_q_31_s1` to `partial_q_44_s0`, with a 25.649 ns arrival time. Regfile-to-data-memory paths follow closely. The small margin makes the measured gain sensitive to placement.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-001-r2s0 (regression, +4.61%): Squashing decode through the ID/EX valid bit cut the EX redirect feedback through IF and hazard logic into the ID/EX payload, exposing the five-step divider update as the Gowin timing limit and leaving a placement-sensitive CoreMark gain at 49.128 MHz median Fmax with unchanged cycle count.

title: Decouple fetch with one fall-through instruction slot
motivation:
The 46.963 MHz champion holds the fetch PC whenever a load-use hazard,
data-memory stall or divide blocks decode. A ready instruction response
during that hold is lost and the same address may face an imem stall
when decode resumes. The champion also replaces the fetched word with
a NOP on EX redirect. Its reported 27.746 ns worst path runs from EX
forwarding through that flush and back to the ID/EX JALR decode bit.
An elastic fetch boundary can save a ready response and squash by
validity, letting decode see the selected instruction word directly.

motivation:

implementation_notes:
# Bench implementation notes

EX/MEM captures the full forwarded `rs1 + imm` sum in `effective_addr` and holds it during data backpressure. MEM uses that field for the bus address, lane masks, alignment checks, load extraction, and the word-aligned RVFI address. JALR clears bit zero on its target path. The existing ALU result still feeds forwarding and writeback.

The divider decodes the leading two dividend bits in the first update and registers the 34-bit `3D` on the same edge. Each of the next six updates runs two radix-4 steps with parallel 35-bit trials against `D`, `2D`, and `3D`, then one radix-2 step. Each radix-4 step selects its remainder with one-hot enables derived from the ordered borrow flags. The hardware and ALTOPS builds share the launch, seven updates, held-valid result, reset, and consume schedule. The datapath follows the proposed design. Directed cocotb cases add coverage for all first-update digit inputs, wide divisor multiples, and an odd-byte store under backpressure followed by loads and alignment traps.

## Local verification

- Verilator `-Wall` lint passed for hardware and ALTOPS builds.
- `formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-retire ALTOPS checks on the first run. The wrapper matched `nret: 1` in `cores/bench/core.yaml`.
- All five cocotb suites passed. A combinational SAT check established equivalence between each new two-bit step and two original restoring steps over the reachable remainder bounds.
- Reference co-simulation passed selftest and all three random programs, each with and without bus stalls. The fitness harness validated all CoreMark CRCs with both stalls enabled and counted 4,191,341 marker-bracketed cycles for 10 iterations.

## Timing and fitness

Gowin placement options 0, 1, and 2 measured 52.133, 53.281, and 53.281 MHz. Option 0 used 3,386 logic cells and 725 registers. At the 53.281 MHz median, CoreMark measured 127.12 iter/s, 11.45% above the 114.06 iter/s champion and above the 4.6% acceptance margin.

The measured median is 2.282 MHz below the scratch prototype. The longest setup path in all three placements runs from the register file to the EX/MEM ALU result register. The divider recurrence is close behind in both median placements.

title: Run the BTB ahead of decode across predicted control transfers
motivation:

47.807 MHz. A replay of its retired control transfers estimates just 57,035

reclaim only about 1.4% of the cycles at one slot per redirect. Today a

can request the target. Let the predictor walk the path while decode
waits on a load-use dependency or EX is held by the data bus. Decode can
then consume those responses when the instruction bus is stalled. The
earlier single fall-through slot saved 3.07% on the nonpredicting parent.

occupancy count and a fixed registered head. Bypass an empty FIFO

Resolve each instruction against its own recorded successor in EX.
Compare that successor with full-width target and fall-through in
parallel with direction resolution, and report the actual next PC to

valid bit on the same edge. Preserve the existing trap and link handling.
An older dmem stall defers EX recovery and training, while fetch can fill
available slots. Apply the same rule to fetch while the divider is busy.
On FENCE.I advancing through EX, flush the prefetched words and resume
at its architectural successor. If fetch accepts the last in-range word
and predicts sequentially beyond 1 MiB, hold the request at that word
and block further response acceptance. Set bit zero in that packet's
recorded successor to force a comparison miss when it reaches EX.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

The 32-entry BTB drives a request PC that follows the chosen successor on each accepted instruction response. A four-entry fall-through FIFO holds the full PC, instruction, and recorded successor. ID can bypass the empty queue or consume its fixed head while imem is unready. Load-use, dmem, and divider stalls constrain ID issue, and fetch can fill all four entries during those stalls. A full queue can dequeue and refill on the same edge.

The instruction's recorded successor goes through ID/EX. EX compares it with the full-width target and `PC + 4` in parallel with direction resolution. A mismatch or an advancing FENCE.I flushes the queue and squashes the younger ID/EX slot. RVFI reports the resolved architectural successor. At `0x000F_FFFC`, a sequential prediction holds the request and marks bit zero of the saved successor. EX's normal recovery clears the hold and supplies the full architectural address.

ID calculates `PC + 4` from the selected head PC and latches a one-bit FENCE.I decode for EX. Registering that decode reduced the timed instruction bits carried into EX by nine. BTB tag and counter metadata have a separate read by the head PC, including the same-index EX update bypass. The target array is read by the request PC. EX qualifies training and recovery with instruction advance. FIFO occupancy determines validity after a flush, and only occupied entries shift on a dequeue.

Directed cocotb coverage includes predicted target prefetch during a dmem stall, full-queue refill, a queued load-use dependency with imem unready, wrong-path store squash on dmem release, FENCE.I refetch after a code store, and an in-range redirect from the last RAM word while fetch runs ahead of a divide.

# Execute forwarding in cores/bench

ID registers source matches against the instructions advancing from EX and MEM. EX qualifies the matches with the producers' write controls and selects from the ALU and jump-link lane, multiply lane, formatted memory response, MEM/WB value, or captured register-file value. MEM selects load bytes and sign bits in parallel, then registers one value for writeback and the older bypass. A pending data request holds ID/EX and EX/MEM. MEM/WB clears retirement validity while retaining its forwarding value and writer qualification. A ready load and its immediate consumer advance together. Misaligned accesses raise the trap without issuing a data request or waiting for bus readiness.

implementation_notes:
# Bench BTB validation across EX/MEM

EX registers the chosen static successor and its match bit alongside the observed full request PC. Validation uses that match for static successors and compares the recorded request PC against the registered effective-address sum with bit zero cleared for a taken JALR. Every advancing slot creates one validation record. The same resolved successor supplies RVFI, and the EX/MEM jump result still supplies the link value.

A miss presents the full corrected address during validation and kills the younger EX slot before EX/MEM or divider launch. A ready corrected response enters ID with its sequential successor, bypassing the BTB for that response. A blocked response clears ID/EX validity and saves the corrected address for ordinary prediction on retry. Validation is consumed even when its own memory request holds EX/MEM. The pending memory request and MEM/WB forwarding data remain available through the stall. FENCE.I forces a re-fetch, and speculative fall-through from the last RAM word parks with acceptance disabled until validation redirects it.

The 32-entry BTB still predicts in one cycle from the ordinary request PC. Training reads the resolving slot's tag and counter through a separate metadata read, with the prior allocation, saturation, and RAM-range rules. Prediction on the write edge uses the pre-write entry.

The implementation also shares one magnitude comparison across the signed and unsigned branch conditions, using the sign bits and `funct3` to select and invert the result. Fetch uses mutually exclusive selects for the two ordinary and two recovery next-PC candidates. These changes reduced the mapped logic in the measured implementation. The most limiting path in all three placements runs from data RAM to the EX/MEM ALU-result register. The register-file path is also among the worst paths in options 1 and 2.

The 212.81 iter/s bench champion runs ten CoreMark iterations in
3,337,377 marker-bracketed cycles at a 71.024 MHz Gowin median. Its
slowest reported placement puts data RAM readback through the load
formatter and EX operand network on the path to the shift result.
The low byte of each formatted response currently uses four masked
data lanes, with separate load qualification for both forwarded
operands and writeback. A single indexed byte selection can serve
all three consumers and reduce the late RAM data routing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the four-bit low-byte mask with a two-bit index registered
with the EX/MEM load-format controls. A word load selects byte 0,
a halfword load selects byte 0 or 2 using address bit 1, and a byte
load selects address bits [1:0]. In the MEM formatter, select
data[{byte_index, 3'b0} +: 8] from the raw memory response. Gate
the selected byte with each destination's existing load-select bit
after the selection, so all three destinations can share the mux.
Continue using the existing registered masks for the upper bytes
and sign bits. Preserve misaligned-access suppression, forwarding
priority, and EX/MEM holds so dependent instructions still issue
with zero load-use bubbles on a ready response.

A scratch prototype measured 73.324, 74.310, and 74.310 MHz in the
three Gowin placements. With both stall streams enabled it matched
the canonical CoreMark CRCs in 3,337,377 bracketed cycles, yielding
222.66 iter/s from the timing median, a 4.63% gain. All five cocotb
suites passed, including signed and unsigned loads across every
legal byte and halfword lane. RVFI cosim passed selftest and the
three random programs with and without bus stalls. The 52 completed
ALTOPS checks passed, with register consistency still pending at
the end of the probe. The gain is close to the 4.6% acceptance
margin. Use the three-placement median and the standard correctness
gates to evaluate the implementation.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

EX decodes the load width into a two-bit byte index and registers it with the existing EX/MEM load controls. Byte loads use both low address bits, halfword loads use address bit 1 followed by a zero, and word loads select lane 0. MEM selects the low byte once from the raw response and applies each operand's forwarding enable and the writeback load select after the mux. The existing upper-byte and sign masks, misalignment checks, and pipeline holds still qualify the corresponding results.

The datapath follows the hypothesis. I used an explicit width case because it produced the fastest median in local Gowin measurements. Placement option 0 reached 68.729 MHz and was limited by the fetch replay path. The divider limited options 1 and 2, both at 75.894 MHz, giving a 75.894 MHz median.

- Verilator lint and all five cocotb suites passed. The pipeline tests cover signed and unsigned subword lanes, both forwarding operands, zero load-use bubbles on ready responses, and stalls.
- RVFI cosim passed selftest and all three random programs with both buses ready and with both stall streams enabled. CoreMark matched the canonical CRCs and completed 10 iterations in 3,337,377 marker-bracketed cycles.
- The measured Fmax and CoreMark cycle count yield 227.41 iterations/s, up 6.86% from the 212.81 iterations/s champion.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-channel ALTOPS checks on the final RTL, including register consistency. The run used an isolated scratch copy of the standard harness.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-001-r8s0 (regression, +6.86%): Using a registered EX/MEM index to share the low-byte mux before per-destination load gating shortened the RAM-to-shifter forwarding path and exposed a divider-limited 75.894 MHz Gowin median, with unchanged CoreMark cycles leaving throughput behind the round winner's stall-reducing fetch replay.

title: Register load forwarding outside equality branches
motivation:
The bench champion scores 212.81 CoreMark iterations per second at a
71.024 MHz median Gowin clock in 3,337,377 marker-bracketed cycles.
Its worst reported path runs from data RAM through load forwarding
to the EX/MEM shift-result register. The round-seven structural trial
reached 79.065 MHz by removing raw load forwarding from the ALU and
JALR, but one placement still timed through the dependent memory
address. That round's trace counted 135,320 immediate load-dependent
branches, 59,270 immediate load-dependent loads and roughly 9,400
other adjacent load consumers. A new marker-bracketed trace classified
all 135,320 immediately dependent branches as BEQ or BNE. Their equality
test can use the formatted memory word through a short bypass while the
registered writeback boundary takes RAM readback out of the arithmetic,
address, store-data and ordered-compare paths.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the existing MEM/WB result register the forwarding boundary for
loads feeding ALU, M-extension, JALR, effective addresses, store data
and signed or unsigned ordered branches. Keep the existing EX/MEM
forwarding for other producers. When a live consumer on that path
uses a source whose youngest eligible
producer is the EX/MEM load, hold IF and ID/EX until the load accepts.
On the accepting edge let the load advance into MEM/WB, insert one
EX/MEM bubble, save the consumer's other forwarded operand and retag
the load matches to MEM/WB. Unready cycles preserve the request and
forwarding state. Guard the replay with producer validity, register
write eligibility, nonzero destination and the consumer's decoded
source-use mask. Preserve both raw source values reported by RVFI,
including source fields unused by the execution unit.

Give BEQ and BNE a direct bypass into four parallel byte equality
comparisons on the complete formatted operands. Use independent
register-backed operands for the ordered branch comparator. Register
direction, target alignment and full-width successor matches at
EX/MEM, with both saturated BTB counter outcomes prepared in parallel.
A ready load and its dependent BEQ or BNE can therefore pass EX/MEM on
successive edges. Use the registered branch decision for retirement
PC and misalignment trap as well as recovery and training. Squash the
younger slot before it can advance or launch a divider. Validate EX
successors against the ordinary registered fetch PC, which equals the
presented PC whenever the EX candidate is live.

Compute the ordinary fetch successor for both possible pending BTB
updates from one ordinary-PC lookup before selecting on the verdict.
Compute the corrected target and fall-through requests in parallel.
Compute ordinary acceptance from word readiness and the normal holds.
Compute corrected acceptance from imem readiness and the older dmem
hold, since the younger EX candidate has been squashed.
When a corrected word accepts, follow its sequential successor for
that beat while preserving tagged BTB metadata for future training.
Under backpressure, carry the corrected address into the ordinary PC
register. Use a late select to send the same next PC to that register
and the synchronous replay read. Preserve pending BTB writes and
same-index metadata repair, FENCE.I invalidation, range and collision
checks, and last-word parking on both the ordinary and corrected paths.

and the three random programs with and without stalls. All five cocotb

title: Keep BTB-armed instruction replay active in a larger store
motivation:
The current 32-word BTB-armed replay window improved the timed CoreMark run
from 3,987,921 to 3,337,377 cycles at a 71.024 MHz median. The backing store
holds 128 instructions, so stream PCs 512 bytes apart can evict each
other. The window also expires after 32 accepted words on long paths
through repeatedly executed code. Expanding the replay store to 512
words alone saved 1.64% of cycles in scratch simulation. Retaining
eligibility over longer streams and fitting more of their instructions
in the store saved 4.35%.

fetch selects a taken BTB successor or registered EX recovery selects a
taken target. Once armed, retain eligibility across sequential fetches
and fall-through recovery. Clear the bit and replay validity on reset

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

`cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv` replaces the 32-word countdown with an arm bit. An accepted taken BTB prediction or a registered taken recovery sets the bit. Sequential fetches and fall-through recovery retain it. Reset and advancing FENCE.I clear the bit and the validity bitmap with priority over arming and filling.

The 1,024-word direct-mapped RAM reads `PC[11:2]` on the edge that captures the ordinary next fetch PC. It stores the full `PC[19:12]` tag alongside the instruction. A full ten-bit comparison between the sampled read and fill indices masks same-edge collisions regardless of RAM mode.

Raw imem readiness selects both fetch readiness and the instruction payload. The bus acceptance term `!fetch_parked || squash_candidate` feeds the readiness mux and helps qualify fills without a replay lookup. Each accepted ready word refreshes its entry while armed or on a taken correction. Replay requires an exact valid tag at an aligned address below 1 MiB. A recovery presents the full corrected PC and waits for imem readiness in the correction cycle.

The RTL follows the proposed architecture. The pipeline tests cover 40 sequential replay words, refresh from a ready response, every tag bit, simultaneous read and fill across the three widened index bits, a collision at a high index, and FENCE.I refetch, clear priority, and rearm.

- Verilator lint passed with `-Wall`.
- `make test TARGET=bench` passed all five cocotb suites, including 49 pipeline cases.
- `formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-retire ALTOPS checks on the final RTL. No formal fixes were needed.
- `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1` passed RVFI comparison for selftest and three random programs with and without bus stalls, plus stalled CoreMark CRC validation. The local build used explicit `NRET=1` to match `core.yaml`.
- `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1` reproduced all three Gowin results at 71.145, 74.271, and 74.271 MHz. The median was 74.271 MHz. Option 0 used 5,249 logic cells, 1,935 registers, and seven BSRAMs. The worst setup paths crossed data RAM into the EX multiply or shift result registers.

title: Make the formatted load the final EX operand select
motivation:
The bench champion runs ten CoreMark iterations in 3,192,109 cycles at a
74.271 MHz median. Its slowest placement runs from data RAM through operand
forwarding to the multiply-result register, and the other placements report
load-readback paths into multiply or shift. The current load formatter
qualifies each consumer's byte and sign masks separately, then feeds the
formatted values into a wide one-hot operand tree. Both the wide tree and
the ALU's immediate selection can be resolved independently of the RAM data.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Factor the MEM-to-EX operand mux around the late data source. Format the RAM
response once in MEM using the registered lane and sign controls. Share
that 32-bit word with writeback and both EX operands. Keep load qualification
out of the byte and sign masks. In EX, form each fallback operand from the
existing registered sources in parallel with load formatting. Use the
existing youngest-writer load selectors to choose the formatted word or
the fallback at the final two-input mux for each raw source operand.

Fold the PC and immediate choices into the corresponding ALU fallback
operands and mask the ALU load selects with the decoded operand choices.
This keeps the ALU path from adding another select after late load data.
Feed the multiplier, branch comparator, address generator, store data and
RVFI from the raw forwarded operands. Keep load-to-use issue, writer
priority, x0, misaligned-load suppression and data-bus holds cycle exact.
Preserve the existing divider handshake and both real and ALTOPS arithmetic.

A scratch version measured 74.380, 75.030 and 75.030 MHz across the three
Gowin placements. It reproduced the 3,192,109-cycle marker interval and
canonical CRCs, passed all five cocotb suites, and matched RVFI for selftest
and all three random programs under both stall configurations. The 75.030 MHz
median gives 235.05 iter/s, a 1.02 percent gain. The 77.69 MHz promotion
floor requires another 0.46 ns off the median's nearly tied RAM-to-multiply
and RAM-to-shift setup paths. Use all three placements and the existing
correctness gates to verify the timing and the cycle count.

# Implementation notes

MEM now formats the RAM response once with the registered byte-lane and sign masks. Both EX operands receive that word, and MEM/WB gates it with its own load-result select.

EX resolves the registered forwarding sources in parallel with load formatting. The final operand selects use a masked OR. When the youngest writer is a load, the existing forwarding controls zero the registered fallback. ALU fallbacks incorporate the PC or immediate, and the same decoded controls disable the corresponding ALU load select. Multiply, branch comparison, address generation, store data, and RVFI use the raw forwarded operands.

The one-hot implementation of the final select improved the median over the explicit two-input mux trial, which measured 75.030 MHz. The design retains the original controls for forwarding priority, misaligned-load suppression, bus holds, and the divider handshake.

The equality lane registers four byte predicates. Recovery reduces them and selects between the BTB counter candidates computed in EX. The single RVFI channel still retires at MEM/WB.

When another consumer needs the live load, the load's accepting edge inserts one EX/MEM bubble. ID/EX retains the consumer, saves its other forwarded operands, and moves the load matches to MEM/WB. Older data-memory backpressure holds the request and its forwarding state. Divider launch, memory side effects, and BTB training are qualified by the corresponding instruction's advance.

Ordinary fetch acceptance uses the unsquashed ID/EX candidate. The ordinary-PC BTB lookup computes both pending-training successors before the registered branch predicates select one. A corrected request can accept on the recovery beat using imem readiness and the older memory hold. On that beat it advances sequentially, and its metadata lookup uses the captured PC and the committed older BTB update. When the correction cannot accept on the recovery beat, its PC becomes the ordinary request for retry.

Replay validity now uses 32 resettable bank flags and RAM-backed bitmaps to shorten lookup and update paths. The fetch bitmap read, replay word read, and PC register use the same selected next PC. A registered write bypass covers both bitmap read ports on a same-bank collision. FENCE.I clears all bank flags in one edge. The first subsequent fill in a bank replaces its old bitmap. The ordinary successor is computed from the current PC and the pending BTB training outcomes. title: Decouple data-memory service from retirement
motivation:
Bench scores 270.88 CoreMark iterations per second at a median 86.757 MHz
in 3,202,739 marker-bracketed cycles. With only instruction-bus stalls
enabled, the same RTL takes 3,011,370 cycles. The timed trace contains
544,852 loads and 139,630 stores. Today a stalled data request freezes
EX/MEM and the issue pipeline, and a non-memory instruction occupies MEM
for a cycle even though the data port could service a queued request.
Gowin probes that removed the JALR target-match path exposed nearly tied
divider and replay paths, so the proposed gain comes from overlapping
work during data-bus stalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give EX a three-slot in-order completion queue and give the data port
an independent request head. Count the EX/MEM ingress as one slot so
enqueue adds no mandatory pipeline stage. Each EX advance reserves
one completion slot. ALU operations and traps complete locally. An
aligned memory operation tags its request with that slot and supplies the
address, store data, byte enables and load format. The oldest pending
memory request owns the bus even while an older completed ALU or branch
packet retires. The registered bus head holds its payload through
backpressure and can be replaced on an accepting edge. When no request
is pending, a memory operation dispatched in EX reaches the registered
bus head on the same edge. Service requests in program order, accept
each store once, and retire strictly in order on RVFI channel 0. Bypass
the oldest completion's accepting response into MEM/WB on the same edge
to keep the zero-wait pipe full. Permit a pop and allocation together.

Forward from the youngest older valid writer across queue slots and
MEM/WB. Capture register matches before EX and use separate one-hot
value paths. An instruction with a true dependency on an unfinished load
waits for that load. Keep the current ready-LW address and formatted
BEQ/BNE bypasses for the matching bus head. Other consumers use the
registered response. Keep completed values available across holds and
retain both raw RVFI source values. If an unused source names a pending
load, retain its producer tag in RVFI metadata and fill its value on
response. Exclude x0 and faulted producers from forwarding.

Keep branch resolution and BTB training on the EX advance boundary.
Carry the resolved successor, trap status and memory metadata with the
same completion slot. Suppress wrong-path allocation, preserve divider
launch and consume, and send MMIO stores only when they are the oldest
completion. Drain older requests before FENCE or FENCE.I advances and
preserve the existing FENCE.I refetch and invalidation. A request for a
younger operation cannot pass an older memory request or an ordering
barrier. Only an accepted bus request can complete a memory packet.
Reset clears both queues.

A scratch model replayed the 2,922,015 timed retirements with one EX
issue, one in-order retirement and one data-port acceptance per cycle,
approximately 22% data stalls and true load dependency interlocks. It
counted 3,115,746 cycles with one slot and 2,999,442 with three. A fourth
slot saved only another 2,980 cycles. The model omits fetch and recovery
bubbles and assumes the accepting load can wake its consumer immediately,
so the 116,304-cycle reduction is a sizing estimate. If it carries over
to RTL, promotion requires a median above roughly 87.45 MHz. At 88 MHz,
that cycle count projects about 285.1 iterations per second. The wider
bypass and queue control can limit Fmax. Verify marker-bracketed cycles,
all CRCs, RVFI cosim, the formal gates and three-placement Gowin timing.
Test full-queue replacement, two writers to the same rd, dependent loads
and stalled stores around redirects.

implementation_notes:
# Decouple data-memory service from retirement

- EX allocates into a three-slot completion ring. The newest packet uses the registered EX result lanes for its first cycle and spills to its slot if it stays queued. The oldest packet alone enters MEM/WB on RVFI channel 0, as configured by `nret: 1`, and can take an accepting load response on that edge. EX can reuse the retiring slot on a full-queue pop.
- The data port uses an independent registered request head and two waiting entries with one-hot completion tags. An uncontended request enters the head at dispatch. The head keeps its payload during backpressure, reuses its register on acceptance, and gates MMIO stores until their completion reaches the front. FENCE and FENCE.I wait for all older requests. Fetch recovery and predictor training follow EX dispatch, and FENCE.I retains refetch and replay invalidation.
- ID prioritizes the youngest matching backing slot and captures a separate match for the preceding EX instruction. EX qualifies that ingress match with the registered writer status. Held operands follow their producer into its backing slot or MEM/WB. A matching head response can feed an LW-based address or BEQ/BNE immediately. Other true consumers wait for registered data. A packet carries tags for unfinished loads named by its unused RVFI sources and records their values on acceptance.
- The request head stores the load width and extension bit and decodes the byte lanes in parallel with the memory read. Fetch replay fills use accepted bus fetches directly, so the replay hit does not enter the refill enable path. The divider can run while an older store waits.

## Local checks

- Verilator `-Wall` lint, all 70 pipeline cases, the ALU, decoder, immediate-generator and register-file suites, and RVFI cosim passed. The pipeline cases cover full completion and request queue replacement, two writers to one destination, deferred values for both raw RVFI operands, load interlocks, MMIO ordering, fences and stalled stores across redirects. The three random trace programs also matched the ISS under both stalls at seeds 1, 17 and 99.
- CoreMark completed with both stalls in 3,104,274 marker-bracketed cycles, down 98,465 (3.07%) from 3,202,739. The instruction-stalls-only run took 3,011,370 cycles. All five canonical CRCs matched (`e9f5`, `e714`, `1fd7`, `8e3a`, `fcaf`) and UART reported correct operation.
- Gowin placement options 0, 1 and 2 reported 68.311, 78.581 and 78.581 MHz using 4,971 LUT4s and 1,270 registers. The 78.581 MHz median gives 253.14 CoreMark iterations per second, below the 270.88 baseline. The worst path in the median placements starts at the request head tag and ends at a completion-slot writer bit.
- Local riscv-formal passed all 53 ALTOPS checks with `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`. The initial Yosys run rejected a typedef passed to `$bits`. An intermediate variant also exposed Yosys's packed-struct function return limitation. Both frontend issues were corrected and produced no counterexamples.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-002-r11s1 (regression, -6.55%): A three-slot completion queue overlapped data-bus stalls with execution and cut CoreMark cycles by 3.07%, a gain erased when the path from the request-head tag to a completion-slot writer bit drove median Gowin Fmax from 86.757 to 78.581 MHz.

title: Train the BTB from committed state at branch resolution
motivation:
The champion sends pending BTB training decisions into ordinary fetch
selection and carries training metadata through ID/EX, with special
repair for corrected fetches and same-index updates. This adds a
dependency from EX resolution back into the replay RAM address.
Doubling the BTB in the prior round saved only 0.22% of timed CoreMark
cycles. Moving training to a separate table read can shorten selection
for the current fetch without paying for a larger predictor.

counter to predict the ordinary successor. Give the registered EX
resolution record a separate lookup keyed by the resolved source PC.
Apply the existing saturating updates to that lookup's matching

advancing EX instruction. Pack validity with the tag and target and

continue ordinary fetch and EX recovery.

implementation_notes:
# BTB training at EX resolution

Ordinary fetch predicts from the committed 32-entry BTB. Each advancing EX instruction supplies its source word PC and training eligibility. IF uses those facts, the resolved direction, and the shared full-width target to look up the current entry and apply the saturating counter update. Taken conditional misses allocate weakly taken, cacheable jumps write strongly taken, and only a matching conditional entry can decrement. ID/EX no longer carries BTB hit or counter metadata.

Reset clears one entry and its counter per clock for 32 clocks. Clear writes take priority and prediction follows the sequential path during the clear. Ordinary fetch and EX recovery continue throughout. Corrected requests still use the full-width successor comparisons and can accept the instruction bus response in the recovery cycle.

The replay bitmap now decodes the slot in parallel and selects one bit from each of the existing sources before the same-bank bypass. This was a timing change to the slot selector. The replay reset, FENCE.I, stall, and collision behavior is preserved. Cocotb now checks recovery during clear and committed prediction during a pending same-index replacement. Tests that depend on a trained entry hold the first imem response through the clear.

## Local verification

- Verilator lint and all five cocotb suites passed.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-retirement checks on the final RTL with zero failures and zero retries.
- Co-simulation passed for five ELFs. Stalled CoreMark reported all five canonical CRCs and `Correct operation validated.` in 3,202,739 bracketed cycles.
- Gowin placement options 0, 1, and 2 measured 78.287, 79.456, and 79.456 MHz. The 79.456 MHz median projects 248.09 iterations/s and falls below the 90.75 MHz qualification threshold. The divider recurrence was the worst path in all three placements.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-003-r11s2 (regression, -8.41%): A separate EX-resolution lookup removed pending BTB write bypass from the replay RAM address path and preserved stalled CoreMark cycle count, with the divider recurrence limiting all three Gowin placements and median Fmax falling from 86.757 to 79.456 MHz.

title: Specialize divider updates by divisor magnitude
motivation:
The 270.88 iter/s bench champion reports a divider recurrence within
0.01 ns of the EX target-match path. The same recurrence limited all
three placements in round 11 slot 2. Two dependent 35-bit subtract and
select steps handle four quotient bits per clock today. A small divisor
bounds the intermediate remainder, while a large divisor guarantees
enough leading quotient zeros to use fewer steps per clock.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the restoring divider at divisor magnitude 2^16. Below that
threshold, keep the existing six-bit prefix and six four-bit updates.
Use two radix-4 steps with 19-bit unsigned trials per four-bit update.
For nonzero D, the remainder is less than D, so the shifted remainder
and each of D, 2D and 3D fit within 18 bits. Use the extra bit for
borrow. For D=0, the narrow trials still produce all-one quotient
digits. Shift the high remainder bits through separately so REM and
REMU return the complete original dividend after sign restoration.

With D at least 2^16, the first 16 quotient bits are zero. On the
existing prefix edge, compute the next radix-4 digit and remainder
from the top 18 dividend bits using 21-bit trials when D is below
2^18. At or above 2^18, all 18 quotient bits are zero and the top
18 dividend bits are the remainder. Then run one existing full-width
radix-4 step on each of the following six updates. Use the existing
full-width final step in both cases. Take the divide operands from
the existing raw M-extension inputs in the split core instance, and
from a/b in the standalone ALU. Apply the same operand routing to
ALTOPS and preserve the phase count and held-result handshake.

The scratch implementation passed the ALU suite with additional
signed and unsigned cases around both thresholds. Gowin placements
reached 76.643, 83.243 and 83.243 MHz. The limiting path moved from
the divider recurrence and EX target comparison to the replay
validity bitmap in the median placements. Stalled CoreMark passed
canonical CRC and UART validation in 3,202,739 bracketed cycles,
matching the champion. The measured clock projects 259.91 iter/s.
Promotion requires a median above 90.75 MHz at those cycles. Run
the unchanged formal, ALU and cosim gates and reproduce the three
placements against the champion.

implementation_notes:
# Specialize divider updates by divisor magnitude

`alu.sv` classifies the unsigned divisor magnitude at the prefix update. Below `2^16`, it processes a six-bit prefix and six updates of two radix-4 steps with 19-bit trials. For a zero divisor, those steps produce all-one quotient digits and shift the upper remainder bits directly. At `2^16` and above, it processes an 18-bit prefix and six full-width radix-4 updates. The prefix resolves one digit with 21-bit trials below `2^18`. At that threshold and above, the prefix quotient is zero. Both modes reuse the full-width final step and hold the result in phase 1 until consume.

In the split ALU instance, division uses the forwarded M-extension operand inputs. The standalone ALU uses `a` and `b`. The ALTOPS divider uses the same operand routing and retains the seven-update schedule. The ALU tests exercise signed and unsigned quotient and remainder near both magnitude thresholds, the boundaries of the 18-bit prefix digit, and held results in both modes.

The first timing run found the six-bit prefix on the worst setup path in the median placements. The revised register input decodes the update enables in parallel with the trials and gates each source with its one-hot enable. The large prefix computes the `3D` trial as `shifted + D - 4D`, using carry-save logic and one carry-propagating addition.

## Local verification

- Verilator `-Wall` lint and all five cocotb suites passed, including 29 ALU cases. `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` passed for all five ELFs after `make bench` built the random traces. Trace tests ran with both zero-wait and stalled buses.
- The candidate and champion both completed stalled CoreMark in 3,202,739 marker-bracketed cycles for 10 iterations. The candidate UART printed `Correct operation validated.` and the canonical CRCs `e9f5`, `e714`, `1fd7`, `8e3a`, and `fcaf`.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 single-retirement ALTOPS checks with zero failures or retries. The register consistency check took 13 minutes and 32 seconds. The preprocessed ALTOPS RTL matches the source staged for that run.

## Gowin placement

| Build | Option 0 MHz | Option 1 MHz | Option 2 MHz | Median MHz | CoreMark iter/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Champion `hyp-20261119-003-r10s2` | 76.343 | 86.757 | 86.757 | 86.757 | 270.88 |
| Magnitude split | 74.153 | 77.313 | 77.313 | 77.313 | 241.40 |

The local champion build reproduced the logged frequencies. `NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench` reproduced the candidate results and reported 4,390 logic cells and 996 registers. The split moved the limiting path to instruction replay in all three placements. In options 1 and 2, the critical path runs from the replay validity bitmap to the replay entry RAM. The candidate median is below the scratch implementation's 83.243 MHz and the 90.75 MHz promotion threshold, giving a 10.89% fitness regression from the champion.
lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-001-r12s0 (regression, -10.88%): Specializing radix-4 updates by divisor magnitude moved the median Gowin timing limit to the replay validity bitmap feeding entry RAM, where the slower post-route path dropped Fmax from 86.757 to 77.313 MHz and reduced CoreMark throughput at unchanged cycle count.

title: Share the registered address path with JALR
motivation:
The champion reaches 270.88 CoreMark iterations/s at 86.757 MHz
in 3,202,739 bracketed cycles. Its median Gowin placements trace
the worst path from registered dependency matches through EX
forwarding, the JALR carry chain and the full target comparison.
The round-11 carry-select trial moved the bottleneck to fetch and
lowered Fmax. A local retirement trace counted 13,735 JALRs in
the timed window, all with a zero immediate. The common JALR
can validate its successor by comparing the forwarded base
directly, freeing the address generator to resolve every JALR
in parallel with validation.

title: Validate JALR predictions with parallel carry checks
motivation:

implementation_notes:
# JALR prediction validation

## Implementation

EX validates the ordinary fetch candidate with four registered groups of independent carry checks. The checks require candidate bit 0 to be clear, anchor the carry into bit 1 from the two low operand bits, and check each transition through the carry into bit 31. Each transition compares the two carries after XORing both with the current immediate bit. This lets adjacent sign-extension bits cancel in the required carry expression.

EX registers the direct target match and the JALR check enable with the parked-fetch qualification. It reduces the four JALR groups in the recovery cycle and combines that result with the direct target match. The comparison registers, including the fall-through match, hold during data-memory stalls. The resolution-valid pulse tracks EX advance and is suppressed during reset.

The ALU exposes the shared addition before the ADD/SUB result selection. EX masks its bit 0 to produce the full JALR target for alignment, BTB eligibility, recovery, and RVFI. The early tap removes the ADD/SUB selector from the target path and gave the highest median Fmax of the local variants.

## Verification

- Verilator lint passed with `-Wall`.
- A combinational SAT proof established equality with ordinary candidate-PC comparison against masked 32-bit addition for arbitrary operands and candidates. It included direct targets and the parked-fetch qualifier.
- The existing cocotb suites passed. RVFI co-simulation passed for selftest and all three random programs with zero-wait buses and with randomized stalls on both buses.
- Stalled CoreMark validated all five CRCs without an out-of-bounds access. The start and stop markers were at cycles 12,468 and 3,215,207, giving 3,202,739 timed cycles.
- The single-retirement `formal/run_all.sh` gate passed all 53 checks on the final RTL, including the depth-20 register-consistency check. It used `wrapper_si.sv` and `checks_si.cfg` in a scratch copy. No formal fixes were needed.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Champion rerun | 76.343 MHz | 86.757 MHz | 86.757 MHz | 86.757 MHz | 4,393 |
| Parallel carry checks | 76.896 MHz | 79.924 MHz | 79.924 MHz | 79.924 MHz | 4,342 |

The divider's partial-remainder feedback limits options 1 and 2. The fetch replay path limits option 0. At the measured cycle count the median gives 249.55 CoreMark iterations/s, 7.88% below the champion. The median also falls short of the supplied scratch result of 82.978 MHz and the 90.75 MHz promotion threshold.

title: Retain held replay words outside the RAM address path

implementation_notes:
# Predicted JALR operand validation

IF supplies the aligned table and pending-write target words with the selection and qualification for the target it actually chose. It forms the ordinary successor while replay availability resolves, then uses the ordinary advance to qualify the hint. A same-index pending replacement suppresses the old entry when its tag differs. Sequential and corrected acceptances carry no hint.

ID calculates the even and odd rs1 candidates for both target lanes in parallel, then selects the pair to latch. The subtractors share the target and complemented immediate terms and differ in carry-in. The 18-bit aligned target word and signed 12-bit immediate bound each result to 21 signed bits. ID sign-extends them to the full 31-bit modulo difference. The registered hint and operands persist across load replay and bus holds.

EX reduces parity-qualified equalities against forwarded rs1 and registers the match on advance. An absent or wrong hint triggers correction even when the actual target equals PC+4. The match also requires a live, unparked request. A misaligned JALR traps and recovers at PC+4. Redirects, BTB training, and RVFI use the full-width architectural target adder. Direct control transfers retain full-width successor comparisons.

## Verification

- Verilator lint passed with `-Wall`.
- All 144 cocotb cases passed, including the existing parking cases. Added regressions cover both rs1 parities, signed and odd immediates, RV32 wraparound, load replay with memory stalls, pending BTB writes and tag replacements, corrected fetches, misalignment, retirement order, and wrong-path stores.
- Selftest passed co-simulation with both ready and stalled buses. CoreMark matched the canonical CRCs.
- A combinational SAT check using the final ID arithmetic proved that the parity-qualified operand comparisons equal the masked RV32 target comparison for every rs1 value, 12-bit immediate, and aligned BTB target.
- `bash formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 riscv-formal checks on the final RTL. No fix attempts were needed.

- The stalled CoreMark run completed 10 iterations in 3,202,739 marker-bracketed cycles, the same as the champion. A temporary Verilator monitor counted 13,735 JALRs, 1,235 absent hints (8.99%), 747 mismatches among the 12,500 hints, and 58,391 total corrections. Zero absent hints had an actual target equal to the live fetch PC.
- Gowin options 0, 1, and 2 reached 80.861, 80.100, and 80.100 MHz. The 80.100 MHz median yields 250.10 iterations/s, 7.67% below the champion and below the 90.75 MHz promotion threshold.
- The first trial selected the BTB lane ahead of its ID subtractors. Option 0 reported a 12.691 ns data delay from EX's registered branch equality into an ID/EX expected operand. The final version moves lane selection after the subtractors. Its ID/EX expected operands and EX match do not appear as endpoints in the 25 reported worst setup paths for any placement. The final median is limited by replay validity feeding the next fetch PC (12.449 ns data delay). The divider result path limits option 0 (12.332 ns).

motivation:

implementation_notes:
# Parallel divider sign correction

Phase 1 decodes the first radix-4 step's two-bit digit locally and selects one of four reversed remainder differences modulo 2^32. The decoder also qualifies the negative remainder lane with the operation and sign captured at launch. The quotient path forms `-upper` and `upper ^ {30{negate_q}}` in parallel. For a negative quotient, a zero final digit selects `-upper`, and an odd final digit flips the high bit of the low two-bit result. Registered operation and sign enables select the quotient or remainder lanes.

The first radix-4 step keeps its existing interface and supplies the positive result lanes. The divider launches, performs seven updates, and holds the phase-1 result until consumption. The zero-divisor quotient and signed-overflow bit patterns follow the existing launch and magnitude rules. ALTOPS uses the same handshake. The ALU regression covers all four final digits with nonzero upper quotient bits, exact division, nonzero remainders, and held completion after changing the input operation and operands.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 76.343 | 86.757 | 86.757 | 86.757 | 270.88 |
| Parallel sign correction | 76.582 | 79.239 | 79.239 | 79.239 | 247.41 |

On the selected RTL, DIV of `0xffff8000` by `0x80400080` retired `0x00000000` and the checker expected `0x00000001`. title: Register fetched instructions before decode
motivation:
Bench scores 270.88 CoreMark iter/s at 86.757 MHz in 3,202,739 timed
cycles. The champion's median placements limit on EX forwarding through
the JALR addition and successor comparison. Replay-to-register-file
and replay-availability-to-fetch-address paths are close behind. The
round-13 structural trial kept fetch and register-file reads in one
cycle and duplicated the reads. A registered instruction boundary can
shorten that path and give JALR resolution a stable younger PC to compare
against after the existing EX/MEM edge.

hypothesis.motivation:
Bench scores 270.88 CoreMark iter/s at 86.757 MHz in 3,202,739 timed
cycles. The champion's median placements limit on EX forwarding through
the JALR addition and successor comparison. Replay-to-register-file
and replay-availability-to-fetch-address paths are close behind. The
round-13 structural trial kept fetch and register-file reads in one
cycle and duplicated the reads. A registered instruction boundary can
shorten that path and give JALR resolution a stable younger PC to compare
against after the existing EX/MEM edge.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Put a two-entry registered instruction queue between ordinary fetch and
ID. Keep the oldest word and its full PC and PC+4 in a dedicated head
register. Decode and read ordinary operands from that register. Capture
dependency matches on the edge that issues the head into ID/EX. Let the
producer accept from the ready bus or the tagged replay store whenever
there is a free slot at the start of the cycle. A full queue drains
before it refills, so the ordinary fetch credit comes from registered
occupancy and bypasses EX hold. One enqueue and one dequeue can run
together at occupancy one. The queue sustains one issue per cycle
when fed and can save ready fetches during an EX hold.

For ordinary fetch, compute the predicted successor independently of
queue credit and replay hit. Use acceptance to enable the PC and
synchronous replay read together, with redirect overriding ordinary
advancement. Retain the current tagged word store and banked validity.
Hold the bitmap or its same-bank write-through snapshot with its sampled
bank-valid bit and the request. Only accepted ready beats fill. On a
same-index word read/write collision, use the accepted word and its full
tag as the authoritative entry and hold that bypass with the lookup.
A tag mismatch is a miss. Ready bus data retains priority.

Keep a same-cycle, bus-only issue path for a ready correction when MEM
can advance. Read the two source registers addressed by the raw bus word
in parallel with the two addressed by the registered queue head. Apply
correction selection after the reads, at ID/EX, and preserve write-first
and x0 behavior on both read pairs. The correction bypass preserves the
retirement gap for a redirect directly to DIV or REM under the unchanged
liveness check. A correction that cannot issue retains its request for
retry. A ready correction consumes that word exactly once and resumes
ordinary fetch at the corrected PC+4. Preserve last-word parking and
clear the queue and replay validity on an advancing FENCE.I.

The successor checked by EX is the queue head's PC, or the next request
PC when the queue is empty and fetch is not parked. Register that PC and
its availability alongside the full resolved JALR target at EX/MEM.
Compare the two registered PCs in recovery. Keep the direct-target and
fall-through checks against the same candidate. On mismatch, invalidate
the younger ID/EX slot and discard all queued younger words. A ready
corrected bus word can replace the killed ID/EX slot on that edge.
Qualify divider launch, predictor training and data-memory requests with
the surviving instruction's validity. Read the head's predictor metadata
at issue and overlay a pending same-index update so a queued word uses
the current training state. Keep the corrected fetch's sequential
continuation and its existing predictor metadata repair at ID/EX.

Restarting ordinary issue after a correction can cost one issue cycle.
At the logged correction count that is about 58,400 cycles before
accounting for the ready fetches the queue saves during EX holds.
Adding all 58,400 cycles would raise the median promotion threshold
from 90.75 to 92.4 MHz. A 94 MHz median at that cycle count would raise
fitness by about 6%. The divider recurrence and additional register-file
reads may limit the gain.

Check Gowin median timing, CoreMark marker cycles and canonical UART
validation. Check cold redirects and FENCE.I immediately followed by
DIV or REM, a full queue through a data stall, and replay fills that
alias a held lookup. Run the RVFI ordering and liveness gates.

implementation_notes:
# Synchronous committed BTB lookup

The fetch PC, 32-entry BTB read, and replay read use the same selected next-PC index on each edge. The registered target is eligible for prediction when its full `PC[19:7]` tag matches and the registered PC passes the alignment and 1 MiB range checks. Validity and the two-bit direction counter come from committed state. Gowin maps the synchronous BTB array into one additional block RAM.

An aligned, in-range taken correction can write a target once per EX advance. On these cycles the read index comes from the recovery target or its sequential successor, so IF compares those indices directly for the sampled write collision. The next beat uses the captured write's tag and target on a collision. Reset clears validity and the collision flag.

EX registers the source tag hit with the training record. Matching entries train with saturating counters. New branches initialize weakly taken and new jumps initialize strongly taken. IF keeps an asynchronous tag-only lookup for corrected instructions. The IF-to-ID and ID/EX metadata paths still forward pending writes and qualify replacements by tag. Ordinary next-PC selection uses committed state throughout.

The RTL retains full-width EX successor validation, last-word parking, FENCE.I replay invalidation, and single-channel RVFI retirement. The pipeline suite covers replacement collisions across all 13 tag bits, adjacent conditional branches, self-loops, JALR retargeting, misaligned targets, and corrections under instruction and data bus holds. title: Carry the restoring divider state in ones complement
motivation:

radix-4 steps finish within 0.006 ns of the limiting EX target match.
Rounds 13 and 14 repeatedly exposed divider feedback after other paths
changed. The timed CoreMark window executes no DIV or REM instructions,

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Store the entire restoring partial word in ones complement, including
the unprocessed dividend and the accumulated quotient. Complement the
ordinary six-bit prefix output at the existing prefix edge. In each
radix-4 step the trial input is then just {1'b1, partial_bar[63:30]},
the 35-bit complement of the zero-extended shifted remainder S. Form
the three low 32-bit trial values by adding D, 2D and the registered
3D in parallel. The identity ~(S - kD) = ~S + kD gives each
complemented remainder. In parallel, determine eligibility by
comparing the 34-bit complemented S with the complemented multiple.
S >= kD exactly when ~S <= ~(kD) at this width. Compare the two 17-bit
halves in parallel and use lower-half eligibility only when the upper
halves match. This keeps the digit decision independent of the
candidate sum carry chain. Select the largest eligible digit, retain
its trial or the input for digit zero, and shift in the complemented digit.

Reuse the first radix-4 step for the last digit on the current schedule.
Select the complemented quotient or remainder at completion. Invert
it for a nonnegative result or increment it modulo 2^32 for a negative
result. Preserve launch, seven updates, held valid, and consume in both
hardware and ALTOPS. For D=0 every trial succeeds, the quotient is all
ones, and the remainder restores the original dividend bits. Preserve
the existing zero-divisor sign guard and INT_MIN divided by -1 result.

taken from the trial carry reached 84.525 MHz median. The divider
recurrence still limited timing. A full-state prototype using trial
carries reached 81.488 MHz median, passed all five cocotb suites and
RVFI cosim, and reproduced
3,202,739 CoreMark cycles with canonical CRCs. SAT proved one-step
equivalence for arbitrary partial words with the registered multiple
equal to 3D. Verify the split comparisons against that same step and
time all three Gowin placements. A 92 MHz median would yield about 287
iter/s at those cycles. This is an unverified target given the near-tied

implementation_notes:
# Bench divider implementation

The hardware divider in `cores/bench/rtl/alu.sv` complements all 64 bits of the ordinary six-bit prefix result at the existing prefix edge. Each radix-4 step forms the three low 32-bit trial remainders with additions and compares the 34-bit complemented shifted word against the complemented divisor multiples. Each comparison uses two parallel 17-bit comparisons, with the lower half deciding when the upper halves match. The largest eligible digit selects the trial remainder and enters the quotient in complemented form.

The final implementation evaluates the second step's comparisons for all four first-step trial remainders in parallel. The first digit selects both its remainder and the corresponding second-step enables. This departs from the serial comparison arrangement in the proposal and improved the measured median from 68.678 to 78.750 MHz.

The divider reuses the first step for the final digit. It inverts the selected complemented quotient or remainder for a nonnegative result and increments it modulo 2^32 for a negative result. The hardware and ALTOPS versions retain the launch, seven updates, held valid, and consume schedule. The signed divide-by-zero guard and INT_MIN / -1 behavior are preserved. The ALU test now exercises values immediately below, at, and above each trial threshold around a 17-bit boundary.

## Verification

- Verilator lint passed in hardware and ALTOPS modes.
- Both local runs of `formal/run_all.sh` passed all 53 checks with the single-retirement ALTOPS configuration. The final ALTOPS RTL preprocesses identically to both checked copies.
- A Yosys SAT miter proved equivalence to the original radix-4 step and the original two-step update for arbitrary partial words with the registered multiple equal to 3D. It also proved the speculative second-step enables equal the enables computed from the selected first remainder.
- All five cocotb suites passed. RVFI cosim passed for selftest and three random programs with and without memory stalls. Stalled CoreMark validated all canonical CRCs and completed ten iterations in 3,202,739 bracketed cycles.

| Original | 76.343 | 86.757 | 86.757 | 86.757 |
| Complemented divider with second-step lookahead | 77.266 | 78.750 | 78.750 | 78.750 |

The final design uses 5,142 logic cells, up from 4,393. Divider feedback limits option 0. The fetch replay validity bitmap to replay RAM path limits options 1 and 2, with divider feedback 0.002 ns behind it. The median regressed by 9.23% and gives 245.88 CoreMark iterations per second at the measured cycle count. The 92 MHz target was missed.

title: Spill stalled data requests into a fixed EX/MEM slot
motivation:
Bench spends 3,202,739 marker-bracketed cycles on CoreMark at 86.757 MHz.
When dmem stalls, EX/MEM holds the request and blocks even independent
execution. The round-11 structural design saved 98,465 cycles with three
completion slots, but its request-tag-to-slot-writer path capped Gowin
at 78.581 MHz. A single fixed spill slot can hide a useful fraction of
those stalls with only local ownership and forwarding control.

unfinished memory operation it owns the port through acceptance.

accepted EX/MEM access as complete and save its formatted load value

only at the oldest unretired position. Reset clears the spill and
prevents stale requests. Check the accepting edge of a stalled store,

title: Split JALR target generation and prediction validation at the page boundary
motivation:
The bench champion runs CoreMark in 3,202,739 timed cycles at a median
86.757 MHz. Its limiting predictor path forwards rs1, adds the JALR
immediate, and compares the full result against the next fetch PC.
The measured 58,391 corrections leave limited upside from predictor
accuracy alone. A signed 12-bit JALR immediate can move the base address
by at most one 4 KiB page. That gives EX a way to check the existing
prediction without waiting for the upper target sum.

# Page-split JALR target and prediction validation

EX now shares a 13-bit unsigned offset sum between JALR target generation and the ordinary fetch match. It compares the forwarded base page with the candidate page and its two neighbors, then uses the immediate sign to select a page match for each possible carry. The registered low match includes the parked-fetch qualifier and requires an even candidate address. Recovery selects the registered page match using the carry and consumes it only for a valid EX advance. Direct and fall-through comparisons still register in EX.

The full target selects the base, incremented, or decremented page and clears bit zero. The page arithmetic wraps at 20 bits. The target supplies recovery, alignment, the BTB payload, and RVFI. The BTB range predicate is computed from the possible pages in parallel so that eligibility can resolve without waiting for the assembled target. Its boundary checks cover both directions of wraparound. Same-cycle corrected fetch acceptance and predictor and replay update rules retain their existing behavior.

- Verilator lint and all 134 cocotb cases passed. The new pipeline cases exercise both directions of RV32 wraparound, a correct predicted page crossing, and a stale predicted page with the correct low offset.

- The unchanged single-channel `formal/run_all.sh` suite passed all 53 checks, including `reg_ch0`. No formal fixes were needed.
